title: Radio basics
brief: Every radio call answers three questions: who you are calling, who you are, and what you want. Keep it short, use standard phraseology, and read back every clearance, runway and hold-short instruction so the controller can catch mistakes before they become dangerous.

flashcards.front: What is the order of an initial call to a tower?
flashcards.back: Who you're calling, who you are, where you are, what you want: "Squawk Tower, Cessna one two three Sierra Quebec, at the main ramp with information Alpha, request taxi."

flashcards.front: Which instructions must you always read back?
flashcards.back: Runway assignments, hold short instructions, and clearances to take off, land, or enter or cross a runway. End the readback with your callsign.

flashcards.front: When may you shorten your callsign to "Cessna three Sierra Quebec"?
flashcards.back: Only after the controller has abbreviated it first. Until then, use the full callsign: "Cessna one two three Sierra Quebec".
"I have received your message, understand, and will comply." Don't say "roger wilco": wilco already includes roger.

flashcards.front: What do you say if you didn't understand a transmission?
flashcards.back: "Say again." For example: "Squawk Tower, Cessna three Sierra Quebec, say again." Never guess at a clearance.
